description: Every hook but human-name.sh runs the boards binary, through scripts/boards.sh or a fleet shim that calls it. The board's hooks are `boards hook <event>` (claude/boards/src/hooks/): SessionStart clears the checkout's focus on every start but a compaction, reminds the session to check the board first and reconcile it before stopping, catches up on release tags and returns cards stranded in Blocked by Human with every action ticked; PreToolUse on the Agent tool binds each spawn to its card when it is sent, the card its Board-Item: line names or else the focus at that moment, and starts work on it; SubagentStart notes the start, and a resume starts work again; SubagentStop, matched to the fleet agents but the lead, enforces the handoff format, binds the agent to the card its spawn was sent for, turns Blocker: lines into Actions for Human and runs the card gate on a coder's or scripter's stop; TaskCompleted runs the card gate on a [board:<id>] task; PostToolUse on Bash starts the test gate for a pushed release tag whose Cards: line names cards, which moves them from Done to Released; and Stop sends the lead back once when its focused card has unticked criteria, unless the board's config sets sendBackAtStop: false. At SessionStart boards-session-start.sh runs boards-binary.sh, which fetches the release build of the binary for this plugin version, and then the board's own hook, in that order, since Claude Code runs an event's hooks in parallel. The hooks module boards-status.ts draws two lines under the prompt in a terminal session, the session's context, model, project and branch, then the binary's download or the cards fleet agents are working on with a button that opens the board's web UI, unless CODER_FLEET_STATUS_LINES=off, and hands the session one line saying whether the binary is ready, downloading or not available and why. human-name.sh, at SessionStart and in bash alone so it never races the fetch, tells the lead the human's name from boards/human-name under the user's config directory, or that none is stored, or that the stored one is unusable (anything but letters, combining marks, spaces, apostrophes, hyphens and an initial's full stop, in 64 characters), and in either case to ask for it without ever passing the unusable text on; it says nothing in a project with no board and no lead in its settings. The fleet's other two hooks are shims onto `boards fleet <tool>`: enforce-disabled-agents.sh denies a spawn of an agent the project disables and fails closed, and main-fast-forward.sh brings the main checkout's base branch level with its remote.
